title: A2 Writing Quiz 7 — School, Work & Daily Routines

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I have already sent the report to my boss.
I have already send the report to my boss.
I already have sent the report to my boss yet.
I have sent already the report to my boss.
questions.explanation: 'Already' usually comes between the auxiliary and past participle: 'have already sent'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I have started this job three years ago.
I started this job three years ago.
I have start this job three years ago.
I am starting this job three years ago.
questions.explanation: A finished time expression ('three years ago') needs past simple, not present perfect.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I was studying when my colleague texted me.
I studied when my colleague was texting me.
I was study when my colleague texted me.
I studying was when my colleague texted me.
questions.explanation: Past continuous (background) + past simple (interruption): 'I was studying when my colleague texted me.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: This term is busier than the last one.
This term is more busy than the last one.
This term is busiest than the last one.
This term is busy than the last one.
questions.explanation: Adjectives ending in -y change to -ier: 'busier than'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Monday is the busiest day of my week.
Monday is the more busy day of my week.
Monday is the most busiest day of my week.
Monday is busiest day of my week.
questions.explanation: Adjectives ending in -y change to -iest for superlatives: 'the busiest day'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: She can speak three languages fluently.
She can speaks three languages fluently.
She can to speak three languages fluently.
She cans speak three languages fluently.
questions.explanation: 'Can' is followed by the base form of the verb: 'can speak'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I have to submit my homework by Friday.
I has to submit my homework by Friday.
I have to submitting my homework by Friday.
I have to submitted my homework by Friday.
questions.explanation: 'Have to' + base verb expresses obligation: 'have to submit'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I should have studied harder for the exam.
I should studied harder for the exam.
I should have study harder for the exam.
I should has studied harder for the exam.
questions.explanation: 'Should have' + past participle expresses regret about the past: 'should have studied'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I'm going to apply for a new job next month.
I'm going apply for a new job next month.
I going to apply for a new job next month.
I'm going to applying for a new job next month.
questions.explanation: 'Going to' + base verb expresses a plan: 'going to apply'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: If I finish work early, I will call you.
If I finish work early, I call will you.
If I will finish work early, I will call you.
If I finished work early, I will call you.
questions.explanation: First conditional: If + present simple, will + base verb: 'If I finish work early, I will call you.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: He suggested working from home on Fridays.
He suggested to work from home on Fridays.
He suggested work from home on Fridays.
He suggested worked from home on Fridays.
questions.explanation: 'Suggest' is followed by a gerund (-ing form): 'suggested working'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I managed finishing the project on time.
I managed to finish the project on time.
I managed finish the project on time.
I managed for finish the project on time.
questions.explanation: 'Manage' is followed by the infinitive with 'to': 'managed to finish'.

questions.question: I don't have ___ homework tonight.
options: many
much
a lot
several
questions.explanation: 'Homework' is uncountable, so use 'much' in negative sentences.

questions.question: I have ___ questions about the assignment.
options: a little
a few
much
little
questions.explanation: 'Questions' is countable, and 'a few' means 'a small number of'.

questions.question: Choose the sentence that correctly uses 'as long as'.
options: You can leave early, as long as you finish your tasks.
You can leave early, as long as but finish your tasks.
As long as you finish tasks but can leave early.
You can leave early as long as, you finish tasks.
questions.explanation: 'As long as' introduces a condition: 'as long as you finish your tasks.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I check my emails before I start work.
I check my emails before start I work.
I check my emails before to start work.
I check my emails before starting work but.
questions.explanation: 'Before' + clause connects two related actions in time order: 'before I start work.'

questions.question: You need to arrive at the office ___ time every day.
options: on
in
at
by
questions.explanation: 'On time' is a fixed expression meaning 'not late': 'arrive on time.'

questions.question: She is ___ the new marketing project.
options: in charge of
in charge for
charged of
on charge of
questions.explanation: 'In charge of' + noun means 'responsible for': 'in charge of the project.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence. (Direct: "I work in the city centre.")
options: He said that he works in the city centre.
He said that he worked in the city centre.
He said that he is working in the city centre.
He said he work in the city centre.
questions.explanation: In reported speech, present simple usually shifts to past simple: 'he worked in the city centre.'

questions.question: Which is the correct way to start an email to your manager about a schedule change?
options: Hey boss,
Dear Mr. Huseynov,
Yo,
Hiya,
questions.explanation: 'Dear Mr./Ms. [Surname],' is a respectful, semi-formal opening when writing to a manager.

questions.question: Which is the correct way to end a formal email to your manager?
options: Best regards,
Bye now,
See ya,
Take it easy,
questions.explanation: 'Best regards,' is a suitable semi-formal closing for a workplace email.

questions.question: Choose the correct suggestion.
options: How about scheduling the meeting for Thursday?
How about schedule the meeting for Thursday?
How about to schedule the meeting for Thursday?
How about we scheduling the meeting for Thursday?
questions.explanation: 'How about' + gerund is used to make a suggestion: 'How about scheduling...'

questions.question: Which sentence correctly combines 'This is the teacher.' and 'The teacher helped me with my essay.'?
options: This is the teacher which helped me with my essay.
This is the teacher who helped me with my essay.
This is the teacher what helped me with my essay.
This is the teacher helped me with my essay who.
questions.explanation: 'Who' is used for people in relative clauses: 'the teacher who helped me with my essay.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I usually check my emails first thing in the morning.
I check usually my emails first thing in the morning.
Usually I check my emails first thing in the morning always.
I check my emails usually first thing in the morning.
questions.explanation: Adverbs of frequency usually go before the main verb: 'I usually check my emails.'

questions.question: Which sentence has correct punctuation?
options: Could you tell me when the meeting starts?
Could you tell me when does the meeting start?
Could you tell me when the meeting starts.
Could you tell me, when the meeting starts?
questions.explanation: Indirect questions keep normal word order and end with a question mark: 'when the meeting starts?'

questions.question: I ___ on this report all day, so I'm exhausted.
options: work
have worked
have been working
worked
questions.explanation: Present perfect continuous emphasizes duration of an ongoing action: 'have been working'.

questions.question: This laptop isn't mine, it's ___.
options: they
their
theirs
their's
questions.explanation: Possessive pronoun (stands alone, no noun after it): 'it's theirs.'

questions.question: Choose the sentence that correctly uses sequencing words.
options: First, check your inbox. Then, reply to urgent emails. Finally, plan your day.
First check inbox then reply urgent emails finally plan day.
Finally check inbox, first reply, then plan your day.
Then first check inbox, finally reply plan your day.
questions.explanation: Sequencing words 'First,', 'Then,' and 'Finally,' organize steps clearly with commas.

questions.question: Every employee ___ to complete the training by Friday.
options: need
needs
needing
are needing
questions.explanation: 'Every' takes a singular verb: 'Every employee needs...'

questions.question: Choose the correct question tag.
options: You haven't finished the report yet, have you?
You haven't finished the report yet, haven't you?
You haven't finished the report yet, did you?
You haven't finished the report yet, have?
questions.explanation: Negative statement + positive tag: 'You haven't finished the report yet, have you?'
